correctness.rationale: Every nonempty antichain of a fully layered poset lies inside one layer. Down-monotonicity of the chain polytope makes the all-ones order vertex the unique forward extremum. Euclidean projection is solved by strict convexity and a unique scalar KKT multiplier. Backward distance is convex over the chain polytope, hence maximized at a characteristic antichain vertex; isotonic least squares pools its selected coordinates with all upper layers, yielding aU/(a+U). Exact comparison of the quadratic forms proves equality for two layers and strict dominance for k>=3; distinct 1-layer case is a cube. Finite computations check 33 profiles but are not relied on as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two canonically embedded polytopes share Ehrhart polynomial and Euclidean volume, so their exact metric separation is a natural finer comparison. The theorem determines both directed distances for every layered width profile, reveals that the symmetric distance forgets rank ordering while the reverse distance retains it, and provides the unbounded sharp ratio sqrt(k-1) on equal layers. These are structural infinite-family phenomena, not isolated low-dimensional examples.
